w: At 9.10 am, Swamishri performed the puja of Harikrishna Maharaj and addressed the devotees gathered for the annual sponsored walk. Swamishri flagged off the sponsored walk organized by the Swaminarayan Mandir to give momentum to its ongoing services to society. The participants enthusiastically filed passed Swamishri to embark upon the 10km route. This unique annual event attracts five year old children, youths and even seniors in their eighties. This year the walk had devotees from Portugal, USA, Norway, South Africa, Kenya and India. The event had a total of 1979 participants. At 11.12 am, to the surprise and delight of the devotees, Swamishri arrived for the sponsored walk. Walking with a large group of devotees, Swamishri and the sadhus chanted the Swaminarayan dhun. For a full twenty-minutes Swamishri walked towards the mandir.

Bal - Balika National Convention During the first full day of the Bal-Balika National Convention, delegates explored the theme, ‘Vicharan Around the World’. Before Swamishri arrived in the morning session, sadhus described the uniqueness of Swamishri's worldwide and continuous vicharan, and discussed in detail Swamishri's busy daily routine within that vicharan. Then balaks and sadhus played a game of musical chairs in Swamishri's presence in which all those who lost the game were required to take extra niyams.
Swamishri also took a ‘Walk Down Memory Lane’ in which he was shown several pictures of himself, sadhus and devotees, and was asked to describe the incidents related to each picture.

In the evening, Shri Harikrishna Maharaj and Swamishri entered the Rath Yatra assembly in a rath. The evening programme was about how Swamishri is the ideal charioteer because of his love and compassion. Balaks showed that Swamishri is always willing to make time for them, and sadhus relayed incidents of how Swamishri touched their hearts when they were children. Swamishri personally expressed his affection for the children by playing a game with them called ‘Swami's Ruchi’, and by saying, “I love you all,” during his evening blessings to the assembly. Swamishri also celebrated the Rath Yatra festival by giving Shri Harikrishna Maharaj a ride on a remote-controlled rath, and guiding a blimp (small airship) that would symbolically take the balaks and balikas to Akshardham.

In the morning, the Lieutenant Governor of New Delhi, Shri Joshi, visited the Swaminarayan Akshardham complex and then came to meet Swamishri. Shri Joshi remarked, “This is an extraordinary project. I have seen all the mandirs throughout the country but I have not seen any place that has as much variety as here. The mandirs of Delvara and Ranakpur are good, but they do not compare with the grandeur and carvings here.” In the afternoon, Robert Blake, deputy chief of the American Mission in New Delhi came to meet Swamishri. Mr. Blake commented, “I was pleased to learn that you have promoted faith, tolerance, generosity and other high ideals even in America. There is a great need for such values today. I believe that you are an ambassador not only for India but for the whole of mankind.” After the meeting Mr. Blake left Swamishri’s room and then said to sadhus, “What I find remarkable is that he is such a great person, but lives with such great simplicity. For me this is truly incredible.”

ds.t: As much interest as in the match
w: Youths who had come from London were talking about the final of the football World Cup taking place in Germany. Some of them came to Pramukh Swami Maharaj to ask for blessings. Some were fans of the Italian team, and some were fans of the French team. The final between the two was to be played that night. So the fans of each team asked for blessings for their own team to win the final. Then, as the conversation went on, they said, "The match is from 11.00 pm to 1.30 am."

Hearing this, Swamishri said, "As much interest as you have in watching the match, have exactly that much in worshipping God too. Keep that much interest in devotion, spiritual discourses, puja, and your rules and dharma. Look, I am not saying no to it, but learn to keep just as much interest in God as well."
Swamishri taught them to balance modern life and spirituality.

On seeing several sadhus gathered before him for darshan Swamishri asked, “Why are you so happy?” Swamishri replied himself, “Oh, you are all happy because the new mandir is ready and also you will get to see new devotees!” The sadhus replied with an implication to Swamishri’s glory, “Who has made the mandir!” To this Swamishri replied, “Bhagwan Swaminarayan, Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj have done it.” In every deed Swamishri’s life resonates with humility towards God and his gurus.
God is The Inspirer

19 July (V.S. 2063 Ashad sud 5), Thursday, Toronto When Swamishri finished reading letters Vishwavihari Swami and Dharmavatsal Swami entered the room. The conversation that ensued pivoted around the unique aspects of the newly built shikharbaddh mandir. Vishwavihari Swami praised, “The Canada Mandir is really wonderful. The carvings and designs are very subtle and new.” Then he added further, “Even at this age you never get tired of such activities. You are indeed very courageous. It is through your courage that this mandir has been accomplished.” Swamishri responded, “The courage is not mine. Whatever that is accomplished is due to Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj. Shriji Maharaj has resolved to liberate countless souls, so it is his work.” Vishwavihari Swami added, “In all things you always refer to Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj; then what are you doing?” Swamishri replied with a smile, “I am endeavouring on their wishes.” Vishwavihari Swami agreed, “That is what we are saying – Shastriji Maharaj, Yogiji Maharaj and Maharaj are not different. They are all one. So whatever that is being done is done by you.” Swamishri replied humbly, “He (Maharaj) is the inspirer in all.”

To please Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Guru Pramukh Swami Maharaj children, youths and senior devotees perform austerities, pilgrimages or other devotional means. The spiritual endeavors performed by the devotees during Swamishri's visit to the local centers are congratulatory and worthy of recognition. It also reflects Swamishri's divinity for inspiring such spiritual efforts in children, teenagers and devotees.
25 July 2007, Toronot

170 women devotees performed a chain of fasts for Swamishri’s health and the successful celebration of the Mandir Mahotsav. A lady devotee took only one meal a day from 19 July 2004 when Swamishri performed the ground-breaking ceremony for the mandir till the pratishtha day.

Pramukh Swami Maharaj had come here for the reinstallation of the murti in the newly decorated, ornate sanctum of Akshardham in Delhi. As the time of this installation drew nearer, Swamishri became more and more busy in discussions about the arrangements for the installation. In particular, Swamishri was kept busy in meetings on many matters, from the seating arrangements for the devotees who would sit under the dome to the accommodation of devotees coming from India and abroad. Moreover, because Delhi is the capital, many national and international dignitaries kept coming for Swamishri's darshan and for meetings. Just today, Shri Rameshji, Chief Minister of the state of Uttarakhand, had come for darshan. He was extremely busy like this, but even in the midst of all this Swamishri never failed to reply to letters that had come from devotees, young and old, from India and abroad. Today too Swamishri set aside time for a letter from Shaileshbhai Halpati of the tribal village of Nanapondha. In particular, he wished to dig a borewell for water near his house and had requested Swamishri to mark the spot.
Swamishri lovingly looked at the map and after two or three minutes said, "Let him dig the borewell in the north."

Rameshji, the Chief Minister of Uttarakhand, came for the darshan of Pramukh Swami Maharaj. He also writes poems under the pen name 'Nishank'. Recently at the Kumbh Mela, when 1,66,00,000 (16.6 million) devotees came to bathe on a single day, he had made very good arrangements. Swamishri praised his religious feeling and gave his blessings with pleasure.

Harshadbhai Bakshi, an elderly devotee from Mumbai, had fallen from his bed. Pramukh Swami Maharaj blessed him over the phone. Recommending him, Swamishri said to Abhayswarup Swami, "He is an old devotee from the time of Yogi Bapa, he has a spirit of service and has done good seva. Look after him, and if he needs anything now, help him."

Today Mahant Swami Maharaj came to the Abhishek Mandapam. After having darshan of Shri Nilkanth Varni with devotion, he performed abhishek with saffron water. Swamishri was requested to sit here to put on his socks. Swamishri immediately pointed to Thakorji and said, "In front of Thakorji?"
The attendant sadhu said, "Swami! The sadhus will stand around you, so propriety will be maintained."
Only then did Swamishri agree.
During his walk, Mahant Swami Maharaj, the manifest Yogiraj, began the Yogi Vani class. In it came the talk: "He will remain in the form of a sadhu for ten or twenty generations."
Swamishri said, "It is not going to go at all. It will only keep growing."

Swamishri had spoken in other words Shastriji Maharaj's famous sentence, "The great sadhu never leaves the earth." There was joy in his words, because making the sentence he has spoken come true is in his own hands, isn't it!
